title: Hold the check until the text is read
statement: Hold the question until a learner reading alone could plausibly have read the text, timed from its word count at a generous reading rate for their age.
example: One review got past a non-blocking reading nudge by clicking Next twice.
detail: A content review of a Grade 3 reading build found that timers on the text could still be clicked through, that a non-blocking reminder to read was skipped by clicking Next twice, and that a main-idea pass could be earned with every answer wrong. Matching a reference player, the reading engine now withholds Next on its book pages until the longer of 4 seconds and the time its words take at 150 words a minute has passed when the learner reads alone, or until the narration ends when the page is read aloud, with the dwell kept as a backstop. The hold is a floor, not a pace: once it has passed, the learner moves on with Next.
against: Neighbouring rulings in the same project pull the other way: a review asking that modelled thinking not be clicked past named "no timers, no disabled Next, no yes/no gates" as anti-patterns (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-devfactory-2026-09-10/REGISTER.md`, line 29), and another put staged reveals on a tap because "A timer also cannot pace itself to a slow reader." (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/feedback-2026-08-06-addendum.md`, lines 310-311). The sources record the hold as built, not whether it makes students read rather than wait. The ceiling of 230 words a minute is stated without a source, and the 60-second cap opens any part longer than 230 words sooner than that ceiling allows. The build shows the wait as a "countdown shown on the door" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-deploy/BUILD-NOTES.md`, lines 70-71), a visible clock that sits uneasily with keeping clocks off untimed reading (the record no-clock-unless-speed-counts). On a page holding a passage that is silent by design, the hold kept a learner waiting about 60 s while the guide's line said to listen to the story, and the walk asked for such text to be exempt or for a line saying to take one's time (`grade3-reading/artifacts/qc-2026-09-30-staging/LIVE-WALK.md`, lines 56-60).

evidence.quote: Self-read dwell door: `max(4s, words/150wpm)` before the check | yes | **BUILT** — book-layout pages withhold Next until the dwell elapses (self-read) or the narration completes (read-to-me, dwell as an untrappable backstop)

Whilst there were timers on text reading before the question appeared, it still seems possible to just click through, and where a "not so fast — read, read" nudge appeared it was non-blocking and skipped by clicking Next twice.
The read-gate is bypassed by clicking Next a second time (the "not so fast — read" step is skipped), and in a main-idea task we earned the pass while answering every question incorrectly.

in read-myself mode the chunk's Quick-check door arms no earlier than `hold_s = clamp(round(60 * chunk_word_count / WPM_MAX), 10, 60)` with `WPM_MAX = 230` (a generous Grade-5 silent-reading ceiling — a faster finish is not a plausible read).
replaces the reference's flat 20-second silent-reader clock on chunk beats
mode checked at fire time, so flipping modes mid-beat cannot bypass the hold
Tapping a sentence in read-myself speaks that one line and never arms the door.
In read-to-me mode the clock is unchanged from the reference: the read-along's natural end arms the door
WPM-based self-read hold (derive from word count × grade WPM norms)

**B1. WPM-plausibility hold on self-reading.** In "I'll read it myself" mode, the advance control for each chunk is disabled until a minimum time derived from that chunk's word count at an age-plausible WPM has elapsed; a learner cannot scroll-and-skip to the question.
Each chunk ends in a RECALL-ONLY stop behind a door that arms when read-aloud ends or after the self-read dwell (`max(4s, words/150wpm)`, PRA-146).
The coach line says "Listen to the story to the end first." The button arms only after a silent timer of about 60 s.
